title.en: Compare quartile and moment measures of skewness

say.en: Income tables often end with an open class like "above 1 rupee lakh". The mean and sigma cannot be found, but the quartiles can. Bowley built a skewness measure from them. In this lesson: Compute Bowley's coefficient of skewness.
Compare quartile and moment measures of skewness.

body.en: In a symmetric distribution the quartiles are equally spaced about the median: $Q_3 - Md = Md - Q_1$. *Bowley's coefficient* compares the two gaps: $Sk_B = (Q_3 + Q_1 - 2Md)/(Q_3 - Q_1)$. It lies between −1 and +1 and is used for open-end classes. The moment measure is $\gamma_1 = \mu_3/\sigma^3$, whose square is β₁.
body.kn: ಸಮಮಿತ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ Q₃ − Md = Md − Q₁. ಬೌಲೆಯ ಗುಣಾಂಕ = (Q₃ + Q₁ − 2Md)/(Q₃ − Q₁). ಇದು −1 ಮತ್ತು +1 ನಡುವೆ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ; ತೆರೆದ ವರ್ಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ. ಭ್ರಾಮಕ ಅಳತೆ γ₁ = μ₃/σ³.

say.en: In a symmetric distribution the quartiles are equally spaced about the median: Q 3 - Md equals Md - Q 1. Bowley's coefficient compares the two gaps: Sk B equals Q 3 plus Q 1 minus 2Md/(Q 3 - Q 1). It lies between minus 1 and plus 1 and is used for open-end classes. The moment measure is \gamma 1 = \mu 3/\sigma^3, whose square is beta 1. minus 1 is less than or equal to Sk B is less than or equal to 1.
say.kn: ಸಮಮಿತ ವಿತರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ Q 3 - Md equals Md - Q 1. ಬೌಲೆಯ ಗುಣಾಂಕ equals Q 3 plus Q 1 minus 2Md/(Q 3 - Q 1). ಇದು minus 1 ಮತ್ತು plus 1 ನಡುವೆ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ; ತೆರೆದ ವರ್ಗಗಳಿಗೆ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ. ಭ್ರಾಮಕ ಅಳತೆ gamma 1 equals micro 3/ sigma cubed.

say.en: Uses only the middle 50 percent of data.
Moment measure: gamma 1 equals micro 3/ sigma cubed.
Mark Q one at twenty, the median at thirty and Q three at fifty on a line.
The left gap is ten, the right gap is twenty. The right side is stretched, so the skew is positive.
Bowley divides the difference of the gaps by their sum, which is the interquartile range.
If the gaps are equal it is zero. It can never go beyond plus or minus one.
On the board: Unequal gaps.

problem.en: Q₁ = 20, median = 30, Q₃ = 50. Find Bowley's coefficient of skewness.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Q₁ = 20, median = 30, Q₃ = 50. Find Bowley's coefficient of skewness.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Q 1 equals 20, median equals 30, Q 3 equals 50. Find Bowley's coefficient of skewness.
Sk B equals Q 3 plus Q 1 minus 2Md/(Q 3 - Q 1).
= 50 plus 20 minus 60/50 minus 20 equals 10 over 30.
So the answer is Sk B equals 0.33 positive skew.

problem.en: For a distribution Q₃ − Q₁ = 40, Q₃ + Q₁ = 100 and median = 52. Find Bowley's coefficient.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. For a distribution Q₃ − Q₁ = 40, Q₃ + Q₁ = 100 and median = 52. Find Bowley's coefficient.

say.en: Let us work this out together. For a distribution Q 3 - Q 1 equals 40, Q 3 plus Q 1 equals 100 and median equals 52. Find Bowley's coefficient.
Sk B equals Q 3 plus Q 1 minus 2Md/(Q 3 - Q 1).
= 100 minus 104/40 equals minus 4 over 40.
= minus 0.1.
So the answer is Sk B equals minus 0.1 slight negative skew.
